messages:
jordan_acme: Hey team, during a customer demo yesterday we hit a bunch of 429s. UI showed credits refilled, but API returned 429 and X-Remaining-Credits: 0 mid-request. Longpoll websocket held open. Can we check reset timing?

maria_support: sorry about that 🙇‍♀️ can you paste the tenant/org id and a quick repro? is this noon UTC or local tz?

jordan_acme: tenant: acme-inc-42. Repro steps: 1) open longpoll WS, keep it idle ~30m, 2) start a heavy generate that uses ~12k tokens streaming, 3) halfway we see 429s and session gets truncated. curl snippet from server side:```curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer x...' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml","input":"<big prompt>"}'``` response headers: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
`X-Remaining-Credits: 0`
`X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000000`

also the web console showed "Monthly credits refilled" earlier that minute.

maria_support: thanks — forwarding to infra + billing. @sam_engineer can you triage whether this is billing event mismatch or edge cache?

sam_engineer: looking. first-pass hypothesis: quota refresh happens in billing service at 00:00 UTC, UI pulls fresh balance, but long-lived session connections rely on an edge-layer token cache that sometimes doesn't refresh until reconnect. that can cause the API nodes to continue enforcing the old depleted bucket for in-flight requests. not sure why it 429s mid-request though — need logs.

sam_engineer: can you grab the request-id from the 429 response and the websocket connection id? that helps trace which serving node handled the chunk. also did the client do any retries?

jordan_acme: request-id: req_01H4Y2ABC, ws-id: ws-7f2c. client retried 2x then gave up. we have logs attached (excerpt):```[2026-01-15T23:59:58Z] ws-7f2c START streaming tokens
[2026-01-16T00:00:00Z] billing-bot: monthly refill processed for tenant acme-inc-42
[2026-01-16T00:00:02Z] node-a1 enforced quota check -> remaining=0 -> 429 on chunk 784
```

billing-bot: Monthly refill processed for tenant acme-inc-42 at 2026-01-16T00:00:00Z (transaction id tb_987654)

sam_engineer: ok that looks like the sequence I expected. node-a1's local quota cache still showed 0 at 00:00:02. looks like the billing write was successful but the quota-propagation update to the serving-layer hasn't arrived before the next token enforcement cycle. the mid-request 429 happened because chunk-level enforcement checks remaining before emitting the chunk.

maria_support: action items? what should i tell the customer for mitigation right now?

sam_engineer: immediate mitigation: force clients to reconnect on refill events (short-term), or implement a soft-fail for in-flight streaming chunks: if refill occurred within last 5s, allow a grace window to finish the chunk and then re-eval remaining. also add retry-with-backoff guidance for clients receiving 429 during streaming.

alex_oncall: filing internal follow-up: SRE ticket SRE-12345 to add faster cache invalidation on refill and a small grace-window for streaming chunks. I'll also add a dashboard alert for quota-propagation-lag > 2s.

maria_support: told customer: sorry, we found a propagation race between billing and serving. recommended temporary workaround: reconnect WS after refill notification or limit single-request token usage to <10k to avoid mid-chunk enforcement. offered to escalate. they asked for ETA.

sam_engineer: estimate: we can ship a safety grace-window and cache invalidation fix in ~2 sprints, quicker hotfix possible if we accept small risk. i'll coordinate with infra.

jordan_acme: thanks. can you please also confirm whether timezone settings on tenant profile could affect refill? customer operates in PST.

sam_engineer: refill is UTC boundary for all tenants (single billing cutoff). tenant tz affects UI display only. the visible-time may show local midnight which confuses customers. we should include UTC timestamp in UI toast — filing UX ticket.

maria_support: thanks all — marking as acknowledged by customer. I'll follow up when SRE-12345 has an update. :thumbsup:

alex_oncall: FYI posting remediation checklist in #eng-oncall and adding repro playbook: 1) get req id, 2) check billing transaction time, 3) check serving node cache timestamp, 4) force client reconnect for demo customers.

jordan_acme: appreciate it, that clarifies things. will relay workaround to customer and wait for ETA.
